question: Is Base UI's one unreachable English string a permanent defect, or an acknowledged bug on a path to being fixed?
answer: acknowledged bug, maintainer-endorsed fix planned, and contributable
confidence_basis: The upstream issue and a core maintainer's reply, read via the GitHub API on 2026-08-10. Not inference.
why_this_file_exists: base-ui-i18n.json measured the STATE of Base UI's strings and correctly called the Dismiss label UNREACHABLE — no prop, no provider, an inline literal on an @internal component. That is true today. It is not the whole question. upstream-policy.json asked the equivalent question of React Aria and found a 26-month structural refusal. Comparing a today-state against a policy-state would have been the comparison's biggest unfairness, so this measures Base UI's POSTURE on the same axis. Surfaced by the user, who pointed at the issue directly.

issue.title: [combobox] Internal dismiss button's aria-label "Dismiss" is hardcoded and cannot be localized
issue.author: vanwalj

maintainer_response.author: atomiks
maintainer_response.quote: We were going to solve this with a translations provider (tbd). A prop can work in the meantime, but one concern is that this prop is something people aren't going to configure themselves as it's very hidden/niche/non-obvious.
maintainer_response.reading: The gap is ACKNOWLEDGED, not defended. Two fixes are named: a prop as an interim, a translations provider as the design. Neither is refused.
maintainer_response.maintainer_mitigation_noted_honestly: atomiks also observes the dismiss button announces its ROLE in the user's language, so a screen reader user can partly infer the control's purpose from position and role even without the label. He calls this 'far from ideal'. Recorded because it is a real mitigation and omitting it would overstate the defect.

react_aria.fixable_by: patching intl bundles — possible, because every string has an address (@react-aria/overlays, key 'dismiss')
react_aria.upstream_path: CLOSED. Zero community locale PRs ever merged; translations are an Adobe Globalization vendor pipeline. Same answer from three maintainers over 26 months.
react_aria.stated_reason: opening locales would make internal string identifiers public API, so every string change becomes breaking
react_aria.consequence_for_lumo: 17 fa-IR bundles patched, regenerated on EVERY upgrade, permanently. The patch tax has no end date.

base_ui.fixable_by: nothing today — an inline literal on an @internal component with no props and no provider
base_ui.upstream_path: OPEN. Issue acknowledged in 5 days by a core maintainer; a prop is accepted as an interim fix and a translations provider is the stated design direction.
base_ui.stated_reason: no refusal offered; the only hesitation is that a niche prop is easy for consumers to miss
base_ui.consequence_for_lumo: one string on Combobox/Autocomplete is English on a Persian page until the fix lands. A one-line PR adding the prop is contributable, and the maintainer has pre-endorsed that shape.

the_comparison_that_matters.net: The i18n axis inverts once posture is measured alongside state. React Aria is fixable-but-permanently-self-maintained; Base UI is broken-on-one-string-but-on-a-path, with the maintainer having already named the fix. A defect with an accepted fix is a smaller liability than a workaround with no end date.

what_this_does_not_change: Base UI still ships NO i18n layer today: no bundles, no provider, no locale context. The provider is 'tbd', not shipped.
'tbd' is not a date. If Lumo depends on that provider arriving, that is a bet — the honest mitigation is the interim prop, which Lumo can contribute and does not need to wait for.
The date family is untouched by this finding. base-vega's calendar is react-day-picker + date-fns, and Jalali there is a separate, larger problem than one aria-label.
